after.abstract: The prognostic significance of tumor mutational burden (TMB) in melanoma remains controversial. One potential reason for the mixed results is that total TMB treats all mutations as biologically equivalent, despite evidence that different types of mutations contribute differently to a tumor's neo-antigenic profile. In particular, UV-induced and non-UV mutations may have distinct effects on tumor behavior and outcomes, but this hypothesis has been studied primarily in advanced-stage disease. We analyzed 656 stage II/III tumors from the InterMEL study to evaluate whether UV TMB and non-UV TMB are associated with melanoma-specific mortality and clinicopathologic factors. Higher UV TMB was associated with improved outcomes, while non-UV TMB was not associated with mortality. These findings suggest that an association between total TMB and outcome may be driven disproportionately by mutations associated with UV mutagenesis. Although this has previously been reported in advanced melanomas, our work demonstrates that the prognostic relevance of UV TMB extends to stage II/III tumors typically found in the clinical context. Whether this relationship reflects differences in tumor neo-antigenicity, immune recognition, or other biological properties remains to be determined.

after.abstract: Background: - Type 2 Diabetes mellites and Metabolic syndrome are global public health problems, and their burden is rising, particularly in developing countries. Metabolic syndrome (syndrome X, insulin resistance syndrome) consists of a constellation of metabolic abnormalities that confer increased risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD) and diabetes mellitus. There are limited data on prevalence of metabolic syndrome in type II DM patients in Ethiopia and in the horn of Africa at large, and no research has been done in our institution on this topic. Objective: - To determine the prevalence of metabolic syndrome and its associated factors in patients with type 2 diabetes on follow up at Asella Referral and Teaching Hospital diabetes follow up clinic, Asella, Oromia, Ethiopia. Method: - Cross-sectional, prospective, hospital-based survey was conducted to assess the prevalence of metabolic syndrome and its associated factors in type II DM patients among those who visited diabetic follow-up clinic of Asella referral and teaching Hospital. All type II DM patients, who visited the diabetic follow-up clinic in the study period was included in the study. 285 participants were selected using systemic random sampling technique. Data was collected from patients and their chart and filled on a checklist by trained data collectors. Data was entered to epi-data cleared and analyzed by SPSS version 26.0 and Odds ratio with 95% CI and P-value of <0.05 was considered for declaring level of significance. Results: - Using the NCEP-ATP III criteria the magnitude of Metabolic syndrome was 75.1% in this study. Among the components of Metabolic syndrome high blood pressure was the commonest (70.9%) followed by low HDL Cholesterol (70.5%), high Triglyceride (46%) and high Waist circumference (12.6%) respectively. Female and Male had comparable prevalence of Metabolic syndrome and the study showed that 55.4% of participants were taking Lipid lowering medications. Multivariate logistic regression analysis showed four factors; frequency of taking Meat (AOR = 2.47; 95% CI = 1.323-4.6), Alcohol intake (AOR = 2.79; 95% CI = 1.146-6.806), total Cholesterol level (AOR = 2.72; 95% CI = 1.023-7.224) and LDL Cholesterol level (AOR = 2.31; 95% CI = (1.029-5.161) were significantly associated with Metabolic syndrome according to this study. Conclusion: - In this study the magnitude of Metabolic syndrome was found to be 75.1% and the associated factors were Alcohol intake, Frequency of taking Meat, Total and LDL Cholesterol level. Recommendation: - Counseling of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus patients on the need of decreasing Alcohol and Meat consumption and physicians need to improve the habit of prescribing Lipid lowering medication. Key words: Metabolic syndrome, Type II diabetes, Cardiovascular disease, Waist circumference, Alcohol intake, Cholesterol level.

after.title: Preprint: DYCAST early warning system for dengue virus risk areas, Ribeirao Preto, Brazil
after.authors: Carney, R. M.
after.abstract: Dengue is currently the fastest-spreading vector-borne disease, with an estimated 100-400 million infections per year and nearly 6 billion people at risk--more than half the world's population. However, there is no specific antiviral treatment, thus the primary method for preventing infection is through targeted control of the principal mosquito vector, Aedes aegypti. The objective of this retrospective study is to evaluate the efficacy of forecasting dengue risk using human cases and an adaptation of DYCAST: a biologically based, spatiotemporal clustering model that proved operationally successful as a West Nile virus early warning system. Results demonstrate that DYCAST provided accurate and early detection of high-risk areas for dengue in Ribeirao Preto, Brazil, including a cryptic interepidemic focus of transmission preceding a severe epidemic. Using suspected cases, DYCAST predicted 90.3% (4,237/4,690) of confirmed cases, with a mean lead time of 66.3 days prior to illness onset. High-risk cells had >10x higher relative risk of containing a confirmed case, and sensitivity and specificity were 83.8% and 72.3%. These findings suggest that DYCAST could be utilized in real time to prospectively identify areas at high risk of dengue, for rapid and precise targeting of mosquito mitigation and public education. Implementation using free, open-source software offers a scalable technological strategy for the prevention and control of dengue around the world.

after.authors: Abrishamcar, S.; Eick, S. M.; Everson, T. M.; Fallin, M. D.; Suglia, S. F.; Chovatiya, J.; Jagani, R.; Wright, R. O.; Andra, S. S.; Boyd Barr, D.; Hoffman, N.; Zar, H. J.; Stein, D. J.; Huels, A.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Emory University Rollins School of Public Health
after.abstract: Introduction: Prenatal exposure to environmental chemicals and psychosocial stress often co-occur in low- and middle-income settings, yet their joint effects on child behavior from preschool to school-age remain unknown. We investigated the joint associations of prenatal chemical metabolites and psychosocial stress on child behavior in the first decade of life in the South African birth cohort, the Drakenstein Child Health Study. Methods: Among 643 mother-child pairs, we quantified 25 chemical metabolites spanning nine classes (organophosphates, pyrethroids, neonicotinoid, chlorinated phenol, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, parabens, bisphenols, UV filters, other biocides) in second-trimester maternal urine and characterized prenatal psychosocial stress as a five-indicator latent construct using confirmatory factor analysis. Internalizing and externalizing problems were assessed with the Child Behavior Checklist (CBCL) at 2, 3.5, 5, 6.5, 8, and 10 years. We fit adjusted generalized estimating equations for single exposures with false discovery rate correction. We assessed the joint effects of the positively associated exposure classes using quantile-based g-computation (QG-COMP). Models were fit separately in the preschool (2 to 5 years) and school-age (6.5 to 10 years) developmental windows. Finally, we tested effect measure modification by maternal psychosocial stress and by child sex. Results: Chemical associations were confined to the preschool window. Three polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) metabolites were associated with increased externalizing problems (2-hydroxyfluorene 1.49 [95% CI 0.37, 2.60]; 1-naphthol 1.14 [0.21, 2.07]; 1-hydroxypyrene 1.05 [0.14, 1.95]), as was the PAH mixture (externalizing {psi}=1.00 [0.32, 1.68]; internalizing {psi}=0.95 [0.26, 1.64]). Psychosocial associations persisted across both windows (e.g. latent stress score and externalizing problems: 1.52 [0.83, 2.22] preschool, 1.45 [0.77, 2.14] school-age). The joint PAH and psychosocial mixture showed the largest effects at preschool (externalizing {psi}=2.15 [1.15, 3.15]; internalizing {psi}=2.02 [0.98, 3.06]), with psychosocial factors contributing most to the joint effect. Preschool associations were present among boys, but not girls (joint mixture, externalizing: {psi}=3.42 [2.09, 4.69] in boys versus 0.74 [-0.67, 2.14] in girls, interaction p=0.004). There was no evidence of modification by maternal psychosocial stress. Discussion: Prenatal urinary PAH metabolite levels and psychosocial exposures were associated with child behavioral problems through distinct developmental courses, with PAH associations limited to early childhood and psychosocial associations persisting into the school-age years. Their joint effect exceeded that of either domain alone, and was heightened among boys during the preschool years. These findings highlight the importance of joint chemical and non-chemical stressors on child mental health.

after.abstract: Abstract Objectives Among people with pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB), culture conversion (bacterial clearance) after two months of treatment is a critical indicator of response. However, predictors of culture conversion at two months are difficult to define and can be context specific. In this study, we evaluated how well two tuberculosis (TB) severity metrics, the chest Xray (CXR) Score and the Bandim TBScore associate with and predict two-month culture conversion. Methods The cohort contained 718 index PTB cases enrolled in The Kawempe Community Health Study (KCHS). We analyzed severity metrics, demographics, clinical, microbiological, radiological, household and behavioral data for their association with and their ability to predict culture conversion. Results Sixty-eight percent of participants culture converted at two months. The highest CXR Score category (odds ratio (OR) 0.51, 95% Confidence Interval (CI) 0.31, 0.84), smear grade at diagnosis (OR 0.42, 95% CI; 0.26, 0.62), pleural thickening (OR 0.41, 95% CI 0.17, 0.95) and current smoking (OR 0.31, 95% CI 0.09, 0.99) inversely associated with conversion. Both severity measures and the most parsimonious model poorly predicted culture conversion (all AUCs<0.70). Conclusion CXR Score, higher smear grade at diagnosis, pleural thickening, and current smoking inversely associated with culture conversion but provided limited utility for prediction. Keywords: Tuberculosis outcomes; Mycobacterium clearance; TB severity scores

after.authors: Schalkamp, A.-K.; Chen, M.-Y.; Ayati, A.; Azzam, S.; Shwan, B.; Lewin, S.; Rudrapatna, V. A.
after.abstract: Background and Aims: Acute severe ulcerative colitis (ASUC) is a medical emergency which requires close guideline adherence for optimal outcomes. However, measuring real-world adherence to guidelines and identifying guideline deviations are labor-intensive. We assessed how well a large language model (LLM) based framework can measure real-world adherence to ASUC guidelines and identify reasons for deviations. Methods: The retrospective study focused on clinician adherence to the 2025 American College of Gastroenterology guidelines on ASUC. A multi-agent GPT-5 framework first reviewed inpatient health records to confirm ASUC status. Then for each guideline, it assessed whether it was applicable, recommended by consultants, ordered, or executed. This system was benchmarked against manual chart review. The framework was then applied to all the first seven days of all ASUC hospitalizations in 2019-2024 at UCSF. An additional LLM assessed clinical justification of guideline deviations. Results: The system reliably recognized ASUC hospitalizations (sensitivity: 0.93) and annotated the guideline cascade (overall accuracy: 0.95, N=60). Across 121 hospitalizations (104 patients), adherence was >80%. Deviations concentrated in deep vein thrombosis prophylaxis (DVTp) and timely rescue therapy. Particularly, DVTp broke down at execution despite appropriate recommendation and ordering, whereas "avoidance" recommendations were followed in practice but seldom explicitly documented. Overall, 62% of non-adherence was unjustified, mostly process delays in DVTp. Conclusions: Real-world ASUC care at a tertiary center was largely guideline-concordant, with actionable gaps in DVT prophylaxis execution and rescue therapy timing. A guideline-constrained LLM system enables scalable monitoring of clinical quality and creates the potential in simultaneously improving clinical care and guidelines.

after.authors: Nair, S.; Payne, D.; De Silva, D.; Zaacks, O.; Spaeth, E.; Atkins, D.; Feber, A.
after.abstract: Introduction Most colorectal cancers (CRCs) are detected after symptomatic presentation in primary care. Because CRC shares symptoms with benign disorders, managing the risk of a missed diagnosis is challenging, and many patients are referred unnecessarily for urgent colonoscopy. As a result, colonoscopy resources cannot keep pace with increasing demand. Simple triage tools that can help prioritise patients for referral are urgently needed. Methods ColoSTAT measures the concentration of five protein biomarkers in a single multiplexed ELISA and was validated in a case control study enriched for cancer cases. Serum samples from two prospective cross-sectional studies and retrospective biobanked samples were combined into training (300) and validation (200) cohorts, matched for sex, age and clinical diagnosis. Overall, 56% of participants were male, and the median age at sampling was 64 years (range, 28 to 91 years). The validation cohort was supplemented with an additional 100 serum samples from patients with advanced adenoma (AA) (50.0% female; median age 63 years, range 44 to 84 years). Results Compared with colonoscopy, ColoSTAT detected CRC of all stages with a sensitivity of 89% and a specificity of 54% (90.3% and 54.3% in patients aged 45 to 84 years). Modelled at an intended-use CRC population prevalence of 4%, the negative predictive value (NPV) was >99% and the positive predictive value (PPV) was >7%. Sensitivity was 90.7% for early-stage and 89.4% for late stage cancers, and 58% for AA. Discussion ColoSTAT is a potential blood based alternative for the triage of patients with symptoms of CRC. By helping to prioritise symptomatic patients according to their CRC risk, it could improve triage to colonoscopy and support more effective patient management. Keywords: biomarkers, early detection of cancer, colonoscopy, colorectal cancer, triage

after.abstract: Human consensus is often treated as ground truth in clinical artificial intelligence (AI), yet greater agreement does not necessarily ensure greater clinical relevance. We investigated how expert panel size, composition, and consensus formation influence the reproducibility and clinical relevance of reference standards across three independent pathology cohorts evaluated by international expert pathologists: 50 transbronchial lung cryobiopsy cases from patients with interstitial lung disease assessed by 27 pathologists, 95 resected lung adenocarcinomas evaluated by 11 pathologists, and 596 images of pulmonary granulomatous lesions evaluated by 12 pathologists. Larger panels produced more stable collective judgments but did not improve associations with disease progression or survival in the first two cohorts, instead converging toward consensus classifications with weaker outcome associations. Groups of pathologists identified solely by their diagnostic behavior generated consensus classifications with differing clinical relevance. In lung adenocarcinoma, examination of cases graded differently by the all-rater consensus and a distinct pathologist cluster revealed specific morphological patterns potentially contributing to these differences, suggesting that expert disagreement may contain clinically informative signals. In the granuloma cohort, a modified Delphi process increased agreement, with Krippendorff's  rising from 0.351 to 0.539, while disease-morphology associations changed only modestly. These findings demonstrate that reproducibility and clinical relevance are distinct properties of expert-derived reference standards. Expert disagreement should therefore not be regarded solely as noise to be eliminated, but also as a potential source of clinically meaningful information. Identifying and independently validating outcome-associated morphological features may enable refinement of existing consensus frameworks, supporting the development of more clinically relevant, task-specific ground truth for pathology AI.

after.authors: Durdurak, B. B.; Marwaha, S.; Stokes, P. R. A.; Morales-Munoz, I.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Institute for Mental Health, School of Psychology, University of Birmingham, Birmingham, United Kingdom
after.abstract: Background Sleep and circadian rhythm disturbances are implicated in bipolar disorder (BD), yet it remains unclear whether developmental trajectories of sleep and circadian rhythms across childhood confer risk for hypomanic symptoms (HS) and cognitive dysfunction. Here, we examined whether distinct sleep duration and sleep timing trajectories across childhood are associated with potential HS and cognitive functioning in early adulthood. Methods Using data from the Avon Longitudinal Study of Parents and Children (ALSPAC), parent-reported night-time sleep duration and mid-point of sleep (MPS) from 6 months to 11 years were modelled using latent class growth analysis. During the ALSPAC study, HS were assessed at ages 21 to 23 using the Hypomania Checklist (HCL), and cognitive functioning (working memory and response inhibition) was assessed at age 24. Results Four sleep duration and three MPS trajectories were identified. Logistic regression analyses showed that persistently average shorter (OR=2.87, 95% CI=1.31 to 6.32) and persistently longer sleep (OR=2.81, 95% CI=1.08 to 7.30) trajectories were associated with increased risk of potential HS, while persistently earlier MPS was associated with lower odds (OR=0.23, 95% CI=0.11 to 0.49). Multiple linear regression models showed that experiencing HS in combination with persistently average shorter sleep was associated with poorer response inhibition (B=36.55, 95% CI=8.33 to 64.78, p=0.011), whereas HS in combination with persistently longer sleep was associated with better response inhibition (B=-125.21, 95% CI= -193.56 to -56.86, p<0.001). No interactions were found for working memory. Conclusions Persistently average shorter and persistently longer sleep duration trajectories were associated with increased risks of experiencing HS, as measured by the HCL, while earlier circadian timing were associated with reduced risks. Differences in early-life sleep regulation may be associated with subsequent risk of experiencing HS during early adulthood and may differentially shape subsequent response inhibition performance. Keywords: hypomania; sleep; trajectories; cognition; ALSPAC

after.authors: Kim, J.; Myers, J. V.; Marks, C.; Slover, B.; Whitley, P.; Chen, X.; Yin, C.; Zhang, P.; Thomas, N.; Huerta, T.; Dawson, E.; Fareed, N.; Fernandez, S.
after.abstract: Background The opioid crisis is the leading driver of overdose mortality in the United States. While overdose deaths have decreased in recent years, the reporting lag in official overdose deaths presents a hurdle in implementing public health interventions to combat the crisis. Objective To address these data-reporting delays and improve prediction during highly volatile periods, we developed a Bayesian hierarchical spatiotemporal model using real-time drug overdose data sources to predict quarterly overdose deaths across Ohio counties from 2020 to 2024. Methods We implemented a Bayesian spatiotemporal model using Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation (INLA). Rapid-reporting surveillance metrics, specifically urine drug test (UDT) positivity rates and Emergency Medical Services (EMS) naloxone administration events, were incorporated as fixed covariates. Models were constructed stepwise by first optimizing the spatiotemporal random effect structure and then sequentially adding fixed effects to minimize prediction error. A rolling training window was implemented and evaluated across different training window sizes. Results were assessed overall and stratified by county population size. Results We found that the optimal predictive model structure consists of a two-year training window, a random walk temporal effect, a structured spatial effect, and fentanyl UDT positivity and EMS naloxone events. Incorporating these UDT and EMS data significantly enhanced predictive performance, with the most pronounced accuracy gains occurring during the unprecedented overdose increase associated with the COVID-19 pandemic in the second quarter of 2020. While predictive performance was highly robust in large, urban counties, predictive capability in smaller counties was limited by low data availability. Conclusion Our spatiotemporal prediction model successfully bridges the administrative reporting lags and offers near-real-time quarterly overdose prediction. The study also showed that integration of real-time data sources is especially beneficial for capturing sudden, volatile spikes in overdose deaths.

after.authors: Strange, A.; Weinreich, M.; Klimovski, H.; Holdom, C.; Daniel, A.; Baidoun, M.; Mahiddine, F.; Wong, K.; Magen, I.; Chen, Y.; Turner, M.; Talbot, K.; Lester, D. G.; Thompson, A. G.; Hornstein, E.; Zhang, S.; Cooper-Knock, J.; Shaw, P. J.
after.abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis is a fatal neurodegenerative disease with highly variable survival, and blood biomarkers beyond neurofilament light chain (NfL) are needed for prognosis and trial stratification. A biomarker of progress through an individualised disease course may be prognostic but independent of the rate of neurodegeneration. We analysed the serum proteome (5,401 proteins) and plasma and cerebrospinal fluid metabolomes (1,659 metabolites) of 94 patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and 39 controls recruited in Sheffield, UK, and replicated findings in cohorts from Tel Aviv, Oxford and the United States (AnswerALS). We defined "disease stage" as the fraction of the onset-to-death interval elapsed at sampling. In contrast we define the rate of neurodegeneration by total survival time or the rate of symptom progression quantified using the D50 model of functional decline. Survival-associated proteins were enriched for stage associations in Sheffield (odds ratio = 5.1) and in the Oxford (2.9), and Tel Aviv (1.6) replication cohorts. Sixty-eight proteins not including NfL tracked stage across four cohorts, implicating systemic inflammation and muscle remodelling; the same biology is tracked by 149 plasma and 58 CSF stage-associated metabolites. Stage-associated proteins that rose with stage also rose with age in UK Biobank (17 of 17 age-associated proteins), and the proteomic age gap rose nominally with disease stage (partial Spearman r = 0.25, P = 0.027; BH-adjusted P = 0.055). Circulating gelsolin (GSN) fell with advancing disease in all four cohorts. NfL tracked disease aggressiveness (beta = 0.56, P < 0.001) but not stage (0.13, P = 0.056), whereas GSN tracked stage (-0.41, P <0.001) but not the rate of symptom progression (-0.08, P = 0.25). GSN explained 10% of the variance between patients in disease stage quantified by survival time and 19% of the variance in stage quantified by functional decline; this is comparable to the variance in the rate of neurodegeneration which is captured by circulating NfL. Accounting for disease stage separates markers of disease rate from markers of disease position, refining both biomarker discovery and biological interpretation in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).

after.authors: Schaefer, A. C.; Boeing, H.; Conrad, J.; Gazan, R.; Gedrich, K.; Hauner, H.; Kroke, A.; Linseisen, J.; Lorkowski, S.; Schwingshackl, L.; Vieux, F.; Virmani, K.; Noethlings, U.; Watzl, B.
after.author_corresponding_institution: German Nutrition Society, Bonn, Germany; Nutritional Epidemiology, Institute of Nutritional and Food Sciences, University of Bonn, Bonn, Germany
after.abstract: Background: While nutrient adequacy has been at the core of food-based dietary guidelines (FBDG) for Germany since their beginning, aspects of health-promoting and more sustainable diets have not yet been integrated into their quantitative derivation. Objective: To consider multiple aspects relevant to FBDGs simultaneously via a multi-objective diet optimization model and to conceptualize an approach to transfer the outcomes into a basis for FBDGs, i.e. food guide and messages, on the example of adults in Germany. Methods: The optimization model included FoodEx2 food codes as decision variables (n = 593, level 4), constraints on nutrient intake recommendations, acceptability, and agronomic dependencies, and a multi-objective function that simultaneously minimized diet-related disease burden (disability-adjusted life years, DALYs), environmental impact (greenhouse gas emissions (GHGE) and land use), and deviation from the observed diet. Ten model variants were evaluated using five different weighting schemes for the components of the objective function and two scenarios. For the transfer, optimization results were first further aggregated, then transferred into circular charts for the food guide and into servings for the FBDG messages. Results: Meeting all constraints, the optimized diets reduced DALYs by 39-77 %, GHGE by 40-48 % and land use by 44-57 %. Compared with the observed diet, optimized diets were characterized by a higher share of plant-based foods in the total quantity of foods (66-70 % vs. 55 %), energy contribution (77-79 % vs. 58 %), and protein contribution (63-68 % vs. 40 %). The optimized food group quantities (coefficient of variation ranging from 0 to 1.0), the circular charts, and the servings showed high similarity across the ten model variants. Conclusions: Our findings demonstrate that diet optimization outcomes can serve as a basis for health-promoting and environmentally more sustainable FBDGs. The model's flexibility allows future improvements in data quality and availability to be incorporated.

after.abstract: The PfSPZ Vaccine induces both humoral and cellular immunity. While T cells are likely critical for protection, previous analyses of antibody correlates have focused on select antigens. Here, we apply a proteome-wide approach to examine antibody responses across the entire Plasmodium falciparum (Pf) proteome. Sera from malaria-naive volunteers immunized with high doses of PfSPZ Vaccine were probed using whole proteome Pf protein microarrays and high-density Pf peptide microarrays. Both platforms identified antibody responses that significantly correlated with protection, including responses to the immunodominant Pf circumsporozoite protein (CSP). Multiple reactive epitopes within non-CSP proteins shared homology with the central repeat and junctional regions of CSP, suggesting broad intra-proteome cross-reactivity. Greater breadth of seropositive responses was associated with protection. Cross-reactivity was confirmed by off-target binding of well-characterized memory B cell- and plasmablast-derived monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) targeting CSP. What began as a search for antibody correlates of protection and potential vaccine candidate antigens led to the surprising discovery of probable promiscuous CSP antibody responses that bind non-CSP proteins. The association between protection and greater levels of intra- and extra-Plasmodium cross-reactivity raises new questions about parasite biology and microbial evolution.

after.authors: Aich, A.; Preiksaitis, C.; Rose, C.
after.abstract: IMPORTANCE Emergency department admission plans usually prompt discussion with an accepting team, but discharge decisions do not routinely involve an equivalent discussion, and review must fit limited time and capacity. OBJECTIVE To determine how much time remains after emergency department discharge decisions and how well simple and model-based rules target limited review capacity. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS Retrospective cohort study at Stanford Health Care's adult emergency department, with 2020-2021 training, 2022 tuning, a 2023 temporal test set, and a 2024 held-out temporal test set, including adults aged 18-100 years. There were 258,247 eligible encounters in 2020-2023 and 77,086 in 2024. EXPOSURES Recorded time from the decision to reversal, handoff, departure, or clinical decision unit entry, capped at 60 minutes. Simulations used fixed 2022 thresholds and daily caps of 6 discharge and 3 admission 10-minute reviews. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES The composite comprised 7-day return ending in admission, qualifying critical care within 24 hours, or death within 7 days. Event reach was the proportion of event encounters selected with sufficient recorded time. Replication was prespecified as a Risk-only minus Prior-visits-first difference with a 95% lower bound above 0. RESULTS The 2024 encounters involved 51,587 patients (median encounter age, 53 years [IQR, 35-70]; 42,333 encounters [54.9%] involving female patients). Events occurred in 1,066 of 50,675 discharge encounters and 1,125 of 26,411 admission encounters. Discharge windows were at least 10 minutes in 84.5% overall and 86.4% with events. Discharge event reach was 3.2% with Random, 5.9% with Emergency Severity Index-first, 15.8% with Prior-visits-first, and 19.4% with Risk-only selection. after.authors: Carswell, T. M. R.; Monkman, H.; Giles, J. W.
after.abstract: Background: Qualitative methods can facilitate understanding of the unique experiences of female lower limb prosthesis users (LLPUs) and inform sex-specific rehabilitation and prosthetic design. Given their underrepresentation in research, meaningful collaboration with female LLPUs is imperative to ensure efforts reflect their priorities. Objective: Collaborate with female LLPUs to develop an interview guide with female-specific priorities and use it to investigate potential sex differences in needs of LLPUs. Study Design: Qualitative research study. Methods: Five female LLPUs were engaged to develop an interview guide, targeting aspects of a user's prosthesis, and physical and psychosocial aspects of daily life. LLPUs were interviewed online and data were analyzed collaboratively using Codebook Thematic Analysis. Themes were extracted and assessed for sex differences. Results: Interviews were conducted with 18 LLPUs (9-female, 9-male). Themes arose in four categories: 1-Prosthetic, 2-Physical, 3-Psychosocial, and 4-Financial Experiences, with sex differences observed in all but the financial category. Prosthetic themes revealed female-specific challenges with prosthetic fit, motivating future research into sex-specific prostheses. Physical themes expand understanding of female-specific ambulation challenges, presenting implications for sex-specific rehabilitation. Finally, psychosocial themes present new insight into sex-specific psychosocial experiences, including frustrations with clinicians and concerns regarding maternity and child-rearing. Conclusion: Extracted themes demonstrated an array of sex-specific experiences, which can inform future research to address sex-specific rehabilitation and prosthetic design.

after.authors: Hong, S. G.; Kim, M.; Kim, D.; Ku, H.; Ko, A.; Oh, J.-I.; Lee, J.; Kang, M. W.; Shin, Y.; Joo, J. H.; Lee, J. S.; Lee, H.; Han, S. S.; Kim, Y.; Kwon, J.; Lee, J.; Lee, J. P.; Park, J. I.; Park, J. T.; An, J. N.; Moon, K.-C.; Kim, H. J.; Kim, Y.-G.; Park, S.; Kim, D. K.

after.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists slow kidney disease progression in type 2 diabetes, and in the human kidney the receptor is localized mainly to arteriolar smooth muscle. Whether these cells and their receptor are preserved in diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is unknown. We combined single-cell-level spatial transcriptomics of 5,101 genes with registered periodic acid-Schiff histology in kidney biopsies from 28 people with DKD, 102 with other glomerular diseases and 24 living donors, and measured 2,531 arterioles and small arteries. Arteriolar walls in DKD contained about 20% fewer smooth muscle cells than those in other glomerular diseases, and the loss fell on cells without matrix gene expression. Transcripts of GLP1R, which encodes the receptor, were detected in 0.48% of the remaining smooth muscle cells in DKD, compared with 1.21% in other glomerular diseases and 1.75% in donors. The glutamate receptor gene GRIA2 and the smooth muscle regulator PRDM6 were also lower, whereas contractile genes were unchanged, a pattern not seen in the other diseases. In an independent single-nucleus atlas, smooth muscle GLP1R was lower in DKD than in reference kidneys, and smooth muscle content fell with arteriolar hyalinosis grade. In human DKD, arterioles lose contractile smooth muscle cells, and fewer of the remaining cells carry transcripts for the receptor targeted by GLP-1 receptor agonists at the disease stage in which these drugs are used.

after.title: Preprint: Preferences for Accessible Health Information Among Deaf, Blind, and DeafBlind Adults: A Descriptive Qualitative Study
after.authors: Roberts, L. S.; Shu, C.; Pizzo, L.; Anderson, P.; Jain, D.; McKee, M. M.; James, T. G.
after.abstract: Overview. People with sensory disabilities (e.g., deaf or hard-of-hearing [DHH], blind/low vision [BLV], and DeafBlind) encounter difficulties when accessing health information. These barriers impede people with sensory disabilities in obtaining, understanding, and using health information. This study aimed to identify barriers, facilitators, and preferred formats for health information to inform inclusive health communication, while addressing the variety of accessibility needs across people who are DHH, BLV, and DeafBlind. Methods. We conducted a qualitative study using eight focus groups and eleven individual interviews with adults with different types of sensory disabilities. Interviews were conducted directly in English or American Sign Language, and recordings were professionally transcribed. Discussions explored experiences accessing health information, information source preferences, accessibility barriers, and reactions to different formats. Transcripts were coded using a hybrid thematic analysis process. Themes were generated through team discussions, code synthesis, and community partner feedback. Results. We developed three themes summarizing user-centered perspectives for designing consumer health information resources. Participants obtained health information from various sources including clinicians, family, friends, internet searches, and ChatGPT. Barriers included information overload, medical jargon, inaccessible website design, and communication breakdowns with clinicians. Preferences for health information formats differed across disability groups. Key recommendations included simplified language, structured layouts, and compatibility with assistive technologies (e.g., screen readers). Conclusion. Despite varying accessibility needs across disabilities, participants agreed health information must be delivered through multiple accessible formats to meet diverse sensory needs. These findings are being used to develop health promotion checklists to enhance accessibility for people with sensory disabilities.

after.authors: Ghandikota, S.; Jegga, A. G.; Karns, R.; Hyams, J. S.; Boyle, B.; Noe, J.; Jackson, K.; Lynch, K.; Dillmann, J. R.; Nasr, A.; Aviles, T.; Denson, L. A.; Minar, P.

after.abstract: Background and Aims: Despite expanding therapeutic options for Crohn's disease (CD), treatment selection remains largely empiric. Identifying biomarkers linking inflammatory endotypes to treatment outcomes could inform first-line therapy selection. We sought to identify baseline plasma proteins associated with clinical, biochemical, and endoscopic outcomes in patients with CD receiving anti-TNF therapy. Methods: In this prospective multicenter cohort, children and young adults with CD initiating infliximab or adalimumab underwent plasma proteomic profiling at baseline and months 3 and 12 using SomaScan v4.1 (7,322 analytes) with deep remission (clinical and endoscopic) as the primary outcome. Rank-based composite correlation analysis identified candidate proteins associated with prespecified treatment outcomes, followed by functional enrichment analyses. Regularized machine learning models were used to derive and evaluate a candidate protein signature. Results: In a cohort of 80 participants, mean age 13.7 (SD 3.5) years, 42.5% female, and 90% White, composite rank analysis identified 73 candidate proteins associated with one or more outcomes. Seven candidate proteins (IFNA6, IGHM, MBL2, UBASH3A, REG1A, GABBR2, and NTS) were retained for evaluation. In an independent adult cohort (n=324), models based on whole-blood expression of the seven corresponding genes achieved mean AUPRCs of 0.71 (baseline) and 0.76 (week 14) for the cohort-defined primary response outcome. Conclusions: Plasma proteomic profiling identified a candidate 7-protein signature associated with anti-TNF treatment outcomes in CD. Cross-omic replication demonstrated consistent outcome-associated signals in an independent cohort. Although orthogonal validation of the protein signature is needed, these findings support the potential of proteomic biomarkers to guide biologically informed treatment selection.

after.authors: Liu, B. C.; Fisher, A. T.; Melbourne, J.; Fereydooni, A.; Berens, P. M.; Lakshmi, A.; Jensen, M. E. K.; Rodriguez, F.; Chaudhari, A. S.; Arya, S.
after.abstract: Introduction: Arterial calcium is widely used as a biomarker for coronary artery disease but is underutilized in peripheral artery disease (PAD) due to challenges in automated measurement. We developed a fully automated deep-learning pipeline for aortoiliac calcium measurement from arterial-phase, contrast-enhanced abdominopelvic CT angiography (CTA). Methods: Two nnU-Net models perform aortoiliac arterial segmentation and identification of calcified voxels. We trained on 56 CT scans and validated on 106 scans by comparing the pipeline's calcium estimation from CTA against calcium burden on corresponding non-contrast phase CT within manually segmented arterial contours across radiodensity thresholds of 100-1,000 HU. Using the threshold maximizing correlation, we performed linear regression with five-fold cross-validation between pipeline-estimated and non-contrast calcium quantities, and risk reclassification analysis to compare pipeline-predicted and non-contrast-derived calcium burden quartiles using quadratically weighted kappa. Results: Non-contrast calcium voxels [≥]400 HU correlated best with CTA calcium burden (aortic Pearson r=0.952; iliofemoral Pearson r=0.955). Five-fold cross-validation of non-contrast calcium volume prediction ([≥]400 HU) from pipeline-estimated calcium burden demonstrated aggregated Pearson r>0.91 for all held-out folds in all regions. In risk reclassification analysis, quadratically weighted kappa for agreement of predicted and ground truth calcium quartile classification was k=0.88 for aorta, k=0.84 for bilateral iliofemoral arteries, and k=0.80 for combined. Conclusion: Aortoiliac calcium burden can be automatically quantified from CTA with excellent reproducibility against calcium voxels [≥]400 HU on non-contrast imaging. Quantification of this important biomarker expands opportunities for improved peripheral vascular disease diagnosis and risk prediction.

after.authors: Park, H.-S.; Yin, A.; Parish, M. A.; Hu, J.; Zou, A.; Pandey, R.; Fenstermacher, K. Z. J.; Rothman, R. E.; Pekosz, A.; Toapanta, F. R.; Klein, S.

after.abstract: Females of reproductive ages often mount greater antibody responses than males following influenza vaccination, but the breadth and depth of these differences, including antibody-dependent Fc receptor (FcR)-mediated functions have not been explored. Plasma samples were collected from male and female healthcare workers (range of 21-48y; mean of 31y) at 0, 28, and 180 days post-vaccination (DPV) during the 2022-2023 influenza vaccine season to assess antibody responses to A/H1N1, A/H3N2, and B/Victoria vaccine viruses. Females had greater A/H3N2, but not A/H1N1 or B/Victoria, neutralizing antibody (nAb) responses compared to males through 180 DPV, with differences being most pronounced among A/H3N2 responders ([≥]4 fold-change in nAb titers). Memory B cells isolated from female responders secreted more IgG in response to ex vivo H3 stimulation than those from males at 28 and 180 DPV. Before vaccination, female responders had greater anti-H3 IgG responses and Fc{gamma}RIIB (CD32b) antibody binding than males, with females maintaining greater responses through 180 DPV. Female responders had greater H3-specific antibody-dependent monocyte phagocytosis (ADMP) and natural killer cell (ADNK) secretion of IFN{gamma} and CCL4 prior to and after vaccination, with ADMP positively correlating with greater H3N2 neutralization through 180 DPV in females only. Among responders, the durability of ADMP, ADNK, and nAb in females as compared to males defined the sex differences in influenza-vaccine induced immunity. The greater Fc{gamma}R-binding antibodies prior to vaccination in females might improve the durability of both neutralizing and non-neutralizing antibody responses to diverse vaccines, including next generation influenza vaccines.

after.title: Preprint: Does educational attainment change the association between meat intake and obesity? A case-study from urban Brazil.
after.authors: Laurentino, J.; Palmeira, P.; Levasseur, P.
after.abstract: Brazil is one of the higher meat producer and consumer worldwide. Recently, the sustainability of the meat market is questioned on regard to its high contribution to climate change and public health concerns such as obesity. Hence, further public policies are likely to regulate the meat market and simultaneously reduce meat production and consumption. However, in the context of middle-income countries marked by strong inequalities such as Brazil, the nutritional effect of such market regulation is uncertain. Indeed, one can hypothesize that meat intake plays a protective role against poor nutritious food intake and weight gain among underprivileged settings. To test this hypothesis, this study analyzes household cross-sectional yearly surveys collected from 2018 to 2023 in the 27 Brazilian State capitals. As expected, multivariate estimates show education-specific associations between meat intake and obesity. Among the most educated individuals, declaring not consuming any meat the previous day before the survey is associated with lower body mass index (BMI) and obesity risk, as observed in previous epidemiological studies. By contrast, declaring consuming meat the previous day before the survey appears to be protective against weight gain among poorly educated individuals. We also observe education-specific meat substitution behaviors that help explain these findings. In facts, meat is more likely to be replaced by sweets and ready-to-eat meals among poorly educated individuals compared to more educated ones. We conclude that, everything being equals, meat market regulation policy might worsen public health concerns for under-privileged individuals. Important investments in the education sector and anti-poverty programs are thus needed to limit the raise of nutritional inequalities.

In facts, meat is more likely to be replaced by sweets and ready-to-eat meals among poorly educated individuals compared to more educated ones. We conclude that, everything being equals, meat market regulation policy might worsen public health concerns for under-privileged individuals. Important investments in the education sector and anti-poverty programs are thus needed to limit the raise of nutritional inequalities.

after.authors: FILHO, V. O. C.; Passos, P. R. C.; Noronha, M. M.; Nohmi, R. L.; da Silva, L. F. L.; Saldanha, E. F.; Leite, G. G. F.
after.abstract: BACKGROUND: Meta-analyses are central to evidence-based medicine, but the R packages that implement current methods require programming skills, and most graphical tools cover only a single study design. Here, we aimed to develop and validate a free no-code application that performs the main forms of meta-analysis within a single interface. METHODS: We developed MetaVidence as a Shiny application built on the meta, metafor, netmeta and lme4 packages, which runs in the browser through WebAssembly and is also available as an R package. Agreement with direct package calls was evaluated across effect measures, models, estimators and secondary analyses, and 12 published meta-analyses were reconstructed. Usability was assessed with the System Usability Scale among researchers who had previously conducted a meta-analysis. RESULTS: MetaVidence performs pairwise, single-arm, pre-calculated, network and diagnostic test accuracy meta-analysis through a three-step workflow of data verification, model specification and results. In three of the five families, multiple outcomes can be analyzed in a single run with the same settings, and every analysis reports the parameters that should be described in the methods section. A total of 6,321 validation checks were performed, and the maximum absolute difference in the reference-dataset comparisons was 3.9x10^(-16). The diagnostic module reproduced the anti-CCP example of the Cochrane Handbook to within 0.0002, and all 12 published meta-analyses were reproduced within half of the last reported digit. Fifty-nine researchers rated MetaVidence with a mean System Usability Scale score of 82.8 (95% CI 76.2-89.5). CONCLUSIONS: MetaVidence integrates the main forms of meta-analysis into a single validated interface that does not require programming. These findings support its use as an accessible and reproducible resource for evidence synthesis, particularly for researchers without programming skills or statistical support.

after.title: Preprint: Patient-Expressed Needs, Burdens and Barriers in Taiwanese Online Health Discussions: A Taiwan-Contextualized Friction Framework Applied With Large Language Model-Based Social Listening
after.authors: Liu, Z.-Y.; Chieh, T.; Kuo, C.-F.
after.abstract: Background: Patients' difficulties with illness and care (not understanding a result, distress, daily restrictions, not knowing where to go, family strain) may not surface in clinical encounters or records. Regulatory guidance on patient-focused drug development recognizes social-media listening as a source of patient experience data, but no systematic framework exists for Traditional Chinese discussions in Taiwan, and keyword pipelines measure such content poorly. Objective: To characterize patient-expressed needs, burdens and barriers ("frictions") in Taiwanese online health discussions with an eight-domain, Taiwan-contextualized framework, identify whose frictions they are, and assess how securely each is measured. Methods: From a 13.6-million-unit archive of the PTT forum and three ask-a-physician services, seeded samples of 9,131 pipeline-flagged units and 1,000 unflagged forum articles (10,130 distinct units) were read in full by a large language model under rubrics for relevance, author (patient or family member) and eight domains: information gap, emotional burden, lifestyle burden, medication experience, system navigation, access barrier, caregiver burden and cost burden. Profiles were reported separately for forum articles and physician submissions and checked against a second vendor, two physicians' independent labels of 160 accepted and rejected units, and the archive's keyword pipeline. Results: Among 2,395 model-confirmed forum articles, 83.1% voiced at least one friction: information gap 59.5% (physicians 86%-93%), emotional burden 39.0%, medication experience 24.1%, lifestyle burden 22.2% and system navigation 16.3%; access barrier, caregiver burden and cost burden were each below 7%. Of 3,105 submissions, nearly all were questions and 53.8% also carried a burden. Navigation rarely concerned insurance (9.1%). Family-authored forum articles (14.5%) more often voiced emotional burden (54.9% vs 36.3%), navigation (34.8% vs 13.2%; instrument-dependent) and access barriers (16.4% vs 4.7%), and patient-authored articles lifestyle burden (24.8% vs 6.9%); caregiver burden came with emotional burden in 86.0% of articles voicing it. Emotional and lifestyle burden were commoner in forum articles than submissions under the model, a second vendor and both physicians; medication experience and navigation were instrument-dependent, and physicians disagreed on cost (32% vs 4%). The keyword pipeline had stored its information-gap output for 29.9% of model-confirmed reference-stratum units and over-counted insurance navigation 2.9-fold; its relevance flag was 50.5% precise for forum articles and reached an estimated 42.9% of patient-voice articles. Conclusions: Systematic listening organized Taiwanese patients' and families' online accounts into eight clinically interpretable friction domains, led by the need to understand and by emotional burden, with family-authored posts more often voicing navigation and access difficulty. These expressed concerns may not surface in routine encounters; they identify candidate targets for patient-centred communication and services, which require evaluation. Some domain levels depended on the reader, and keyword pipelines missed or distorted them, so such work needs full-text reading, explicit definitions and clinician checks. Keywords: social media; patient experience data; patient-focused drug development; unmet needs; caregivers; natural language processing; large language models; content analysis; Taiwan; national health insurance

after.title: Preprint: Patient- and Family-Expressed Needs and Burdens in Kidney-Related Online Discussions in Taiwan: Large Language Model-Based Analysis Across Clinical Contexts
after.authors: Liu, Z.-Y.; Hung, Y.-C.; Kuo, C.-F.
after.abstract: Introduction: What people with kidney concerns or disease and their families struggle with between visits may not surface in clinic. We mapped the needs and burdens they express online by clinical context and author. Methods: A large language model read all 22,170 posts reached by a chronic kidney disease tag or kidney lexicon on a Taiwanese forum and 3 ask-a-physician services (1995-2026), applying a companion friction framework with kidney-specific fields, author (patient or family) and clinical context. A second vendor re-read 11,010 posts; 2 physicians labelled relevance, author and context in 200. Results: Among 6,023 kidney-related posts, the reproducibly measured fields most often voiced on the forum were information needs (79%), emotional burden (48%), system navigation (34%) and worry about progression (24%). After abnormal tests, 54%-56% of posts quoted a laboratory value, nearly always with a question or stated uncertainty; renal-diet burden peaked with diagnosed disease; caregiver burden rose to 29% of dialysis-or-transplantation forum posts. Family-written posts more often voiced navigation difficulty and caregiver burden. Most fields agreed with the second vendor (kappa 0.65-0.98). On the model's labels, family members wrote 25% of forum posts about kidney concerns and 74% about dialysis or transplantation; on a 139-post sample, physicians' labels gave 47%-48% for dialysis or transplantation (model 71%). Conclusion: Kidney-related posts carry context-specific information needs and emotional and practical burdens, many voiced by relatives. They suggest candidate responses (test-result explanation, diet support, family-directed information and support) that need evaluation. Keywords: chronic kidney disease; dialysis; patient experience; caregivers; social media; large language models

after.title: Preprint: ClinDataBench: Benchmarking Large Language Model Agents in Clinical Trial Analysis Dataset Construction
after.authors: Li, Z.; Luo, Y.; Feng, Y.; Xu, J.
after.abstract: A new drug reaches patients only after the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has reviewed its trial evidence, which every application carries as analysis datasets in the Clinical Data Interchange Standards Consortium (CDISC) Analysis Data Model (ADaM) format that programmers derive by hand from raw trial data, a statistical analysis plan (SAP) and dataset specifications. Coding agents built on large language models (LLMs) could take over this work, and a slow-changing industry will adopt them only with evidence of what they get right and wrong. However, work on large language models (LLMs) for CDISC data stops short of evaluating a complete, conformant and reproducible package, and the standard validator checks structure rather than whether each value is derived correctly. We introduce ClinDataBench, built on the public CDISC pilot study: an agent receives 22 Study Data Tabulation Model (SDTM) domains, the statistical analysis plan (SAP) and specifications, and must deliver 13 Analysis Data Model (ADaM) datasets, Define-XML metadata and a program that rebuilds them offline. Agents run in containers whose only network route is their model API, restricting online access to published reference outputs during execution. A host-only evaluator scores conformance under the Pinnacle 21 Community (P21) validator, selected derivations, clean reconstruction and effort separately. We compare three settings: Base, which submits the agent's first package; Self-Refine, which revises it without external validation feedback; and CRITIC, which revises it with the agent's own validator report. In an exploratory pilot with six models, the three closed models and DeepSeek delivered all 13 datasets in every setting and eleven of their twelve packages rebuilt semantically, while two other open-weight models delivered no complete package. Validator findings ranged from 15 to 64 dataset-rule pairs. Four of six CRITIC workflows had usable validator comparisons, and each reduced its finding count. None reduced its failed derivation count. The package with the fewest findings carried none of the 234 efficacy summary records in the form the specifications define, showing that lower validator finding counts do not necessarily indicate more correct derivations.

after.authors: Hokororo, J. C.
after.author_corresponding_institution: United Republic of Tanzania Ministry of Health
after.abstract: Tanzania has recently set up a syndromic surveillance of Surgical Site Infections (SSIs) system with the aim to determine the burden of SSI in the country. This study Assessed the Use and Usefulness of it for Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) improvement in health facilities of Tanzania. The study utilized the classic Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) adapted specifically for healthcare information systems; the research team developed semi-structured Key Informants Interview (KII) guides. The QIT members were purposefully selected as KIIs in PHFs. Data collection continued until saturation was achieved, ultimately gathering insights from a total of 49 participants across 20 PHFs in Tanzania from September to November 2025. The interviews were audio-recorded and lasted for around 60 minutes. Privacy was ensured by conducting the interview in an isolated room. Textual data were coded and categorized using NVivo version 20.2 (NVivo.exe). The QIT members reported their perception that syndromic surveillance helped to track SSIs, helped to get burden and trends, and were useful for planning. Participants generally liked the syndromic surveillance and reported using them to inform program design, guide development of intervention and enhance personal knowledge. The participants shared important feedback to improve the syndromic surveillance, particularly as a need to enhance improvement of IPC. Tanzanias syndromic surveillance system use for tracking SSIs in primary care is recognized by QIT as a transformative tool for mapping SSI burdens and informing strategic planning. To ensure long term success, stakeholders must address feedback by strengthening quality of data, providing continuous training, and adapting the system to meet local needs. The overall results of this study showed the importance of conducting syndromic surveillance in order to understand the burden of SSI so as to come up with mitigation strategies of improving IPC across the health system.

after.title: Preprint: lncSigAML: An AI-derived Long Non-coding RNA Prognostic Signature with Multi-Cohort Validation across 2,681 Patients with Acute Myeloid Leukemia
after.authors: Trinh, L. T.; Nguyen, T.-A.; Le, M.-K.; Nguyen, T.-H.; Bekiranov, S.; Hoang, D.-T.; Trinh, B.
after.author_corresponding_institution: University of Virginia School of Medicine
after.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is clinically and genetically heterogeneous. Current risk stratification systems based on cytogenetic and genetic abnormalities do not fully capture prognostic heterogeneity, particularly among intermediate-risk patients. Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) have emerged as key regulators of AML biology, contributing to leukemogenesis, impaired differentiation, apoptosis resistance, and treatment response. In this study, we developed we developed a bone marrow-derived lncRNA prognostic signature, termed lncSigAML, using in pediatric samples from TARGET-AML (n = 1,594) and validated it in four bone marrow and peripheral blood datasets from TARGET-AML, Beat AML, and TCGA-LAML (n = 1,087). Ten lncRNAs were selected: MEF2C-AS1, LINC00477, PROSER2-AS1, LINC01122, KCNJ2-AS1, LINC01108, AP001042.1, SOCS2-AS1, ST3GAL6-AS1, and LINC00355. Among candidate models, random survival forest achieved the best performance and significantly stratified patients into high- and low-risk groups (cross-validated HR = 2.87, 95%CI: 2.43-3.4; P < 0.001) in TARGET-AML bone marrow samples, with stable prognostic performance over 1-, 3-, and 5- year follow-up. The lncSigAML signature also robustly demonstrates significant prognostic effects across all cross-cohort and cross-tissue datasets separately (pooled HR = 2.91; 95%CI = 2.31-3.68; P <0.001). Meta-analysis showed substantially higher pooled 1-, 3-, and 5-year overall survival in the low-risk group than in the high-risk group (80.5%, 63.4%, and 55.3% vs. 52.1%, 28.1%, and 23.9%, respectively). Multivariable Cox regression demonstrated that lncSigAML provided prognostic information beyond clinical variables, genetic subtypes, and cytogenetic risk, with significant incremental prognostic value by partial likelihood ratio testing. Pathway analysis showed enrichment of genes related to cell survival and proliferation, impaired immune surveillance, and aggressive AML biology in the high-risk group, including STK33-, IL2-, and PTEN-associated pathways. To support clinical and research applications, we implemented lncSigAML as an interactive, publicly accessible web application for individualized prognostic estimation. Prospective validation and functional studies of the identified lncRNAs will further evaluate their potential utility in precision AML care.

after.abstract: Background. Oral pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) is highly effective for preventing HIV acquisition when used consistently, but uptake and persistence remain suboptimal among gay men and other men who have sex with men (MSM) in South Africa. We examined client and provider perspectives on PrEP uptake and persistence. Methods. Between September and December 2022, we conducted three focus group discussions with 16 HIV-negative MSM eligible for, but not using, PrEP and six key informant interviews with PrEP providers at a specialized key population health clinic in Cape Town, South Africa. We analyzed transcripts thematically, using deductive codes informed by the PrEP cascade and the COM-B (capability, opportunity, motivation) model, plus inductive codes for emerging issues. Results. Five themes emerged. Limited knowledge, misconceptions about PrEP and antiretroviral therapy, and low perceived risk reduced clients capability to make informed decisions about PrEP. HIV- and sexuality-related stigma, concerns about disclosure, and social surveillance were socially costly. Distance, transport costs, work commitments, clinic hours, and visit burden limited physical opportunity, whereas free care, short visits, reminders, and multi-month dispensing facilitated access. Daily pill-taking, side effects, forgetfulness, and changing sexual activity complicated persistence; routines, reminders, and acceptable PrEP modalities supported continued use. Non-judgmental, MSM-affirming services, counseling, and trusted providers fostered motivation by strengthening clients sense of safety, agency, and control. Conclusion. PrEP delivery for MSM should extend beyond medication provision and address knowledge, stigma, service convenience, and motivation. Low-intensity adaptations, including tailored counseling, affirming care, flexible multi-month dispensing, and reminders, may improve uptake and persistence.

after.abstract: Introduction Transgender women experience stigma related to both gender identity and sexual behavior, yet robust measurement tools remain limited. This study evaluated the factor structure and external construct validity of the Measures of Attributional Stigma for gender identity (MAS-GI) and sexual behavior (MAS-SB) among transgender women in the United States. Methods We analyzed cross-sectional data from the Transgender Womens Internet Survey and Testing (TWIST) platform collected from 2023-2025 (N=2,901). Participants completed parallel 14-item stigma measures attributed separately to gender identity and sexual behavior. The sample was split into exploratory factor analysis (EFA; n=1,951; 2023-2024) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA; n=950; 2024-2025) samples. External construct validity was evaluated via associations with depression symptoms, posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD), social capital, transgender identity pride, and healthcare utilization. Results EFA identified three MAS-GI factors (family stigma, anticipated healthcare stigma, and enacted social stigma) and two MAS-SB factors (global healthcare stigma and social/institutional stigma). CFA confirmed both structures with good to excellent model fit. All stigma dimensions were positively associated with depression and PTSD. Anticipated healthcare and enacted social stigma from the MAS-GI and both MAS-SB dimensions were negatively associated with social capital. Greater anticipated gender identity healthcare stigma associated with lower transgender identity pride. Several stigma dimensions were also positively associated with HIV/STI testing, PrEP use, and mental healthcare utilization. Conclusions The MAS-GI and MAS-SB demonstrate factorial validity and preliminary external construct validity among transgender women. These measures enable precise assessment of stigma by attribution and source and inform stigma surveillance and intervention evaluation.

after.authors: Mecha, J. O.; Muhua, G. O.; Githua, J.; N. Escudero, J.; Kijaro, L.; N. Njagi, L.; John-Stewart, G.; Maleche-Obimbo, E.; Nduba, V.; M. LaCourse, S.; Y.T. Inoue, L.
after.abstract: Background: Pediatric tuberculosis (TB) remains difficult to diagnose. Culture, the gold standard, has limited sensitivity in children (~40-60%). We analyzed 452 symptomatic children [≤]15 years who underwent chest x-ray (CXR), respiratory sample testing with Xpert Ultra, smear microscopy and culture, tuberculin skin test (TST), and interferon gamma release assay (IGRA) in Nairobi, Kenya. Methods: Three Bayesian latent class models (BLCMs) were used: Model 1 assumed conditional test independence; Model 2 incorporated random effects to account for shared biological (Smear, geneXpert Ultra/RIF and culture) or immunologic (IGRA, TST) test dependence; Model 3 extended Model 2 by adjusting for clinical covariates and NIH TB signs and symptoms. We estimated TB prevalence, test sensitivities/specificities and covariate effects. Results: Prevalence estimates under Models 1 [20.2% (15.9-24.7)] and 2 [24.5% (19.6-30.0)] were higher than under Model 3 [14.8% (11.0-19.3)]. All the three model-based prevalence estimates were considerably higher than the 9.9% of children identified through microbiological testing alone. Sensitivity and specificity were broadly consistent across models. Model 3 was considered preferred because it accounted for dependence among the tests and adjusted prevalence and sensitivity for clinical covariates. Under this Model 3, culture and GeneXpert MTB/RIF Ultra demonstrated moderate sensitivity (56.9% and 63.2%, respectively), while smear microscopy showed lower sensitivity (29.8%). CXR achieved moderate sensitivity (79.7%) but limited specificity (40.2%). IGRA and TST displayed sensitivities of 63.7% and 50.1%, and specificities of 81.5% and 65.8%. Older age was positively associated with TB (log-odds ratio 1.09; 95% CrI: 0.14-2.18).   Conclusion: BLCMs estimated TB prevalence and test accuracies without a gold standard. Sensitivity analyses confirmed robustness to priors. Radiography demonstrated moderate sensitivity while culture and GeneXpert retained excellent specificity with improved test performance with older age.

after.authors: Koross, A. K.; Shisanya, M. S.; Kandagor, E.; Kosgei, D.; Jepkosgei, V.
after.abstract: Cyberbullying research is constrained by inconsistent measurement, and the instruments most widely used were developed and validated in European and Asian school samples rather than in African higher-education settings. This study evaluated the factor structure, reliability, construct validity and sex measurement invariance of a 22-item measure of cybervictimisation and cyberperpetration based on the European Cyberbullying Intervention Project Questionnaire among health-professions students in Kenya. In a multicampus cross-sectional survey conducted between September and November 2025, 406 students (215 women, 191 men) enrolled at Kenya Medical Training College campuses completed 11 victimisation and 11 perpetration items together with measures of depression, anxiety and stress symptoms, problematic social-media use, self-esteem and well-being. Items were modelled as ordered categorical indicators by confirmatory factor analysis with the WLSMV estimator. A one-factor model was compared with a correlated two-factor model; reliability was estimated using ordinal alpha, McDonald's omega and composite reliability; convergent validity used Spearman correlations with bootstrap intervals and Holm adjustment; and invariance across sex was tested sequentially. Every item showed a pronounced floor effect. The correlated two-factor model fitted markedly better than the one-factor model (scaled difference {chi}{superscript 2}(1) = 48.06, p < .001) and, after three content-matched residual covariances were released, fitted the data well (CFI = .984, TLI = .982, RMSEA = .049, 90% CI .042 to .056, SRMR = .044). Standardised loadings ranged from .627 to .928, and the latent correlation between dimensions was .849 (95% CI .803 to .895). Omega was .951 for cybervictimisation and .975 for cyberperpetration. Both dimensions correlated positively with distress and problematic social-media use and negatively with self-esteem, but showed negligible correlations with well-being. Configural, threshold and loading invariance across sex were supported. The findings support scoring the instrument as two reliable, sex-comparable but strongly overlapping dimensions.

after.authors: Kariuki, T.; Kariuki, J.; Mogere, D.; Onyancha, J.; Moriasi, G.
after.abstract: Girls who become pregnant during adolescence in sub-Saharan Africa carry a high burden of depressive symptoms. Kenyan studies have relied on antenatal clinic samples and have not looked at stigma, the response to pregnancy disclosure and economic circumstances in the same analysis. We assessed how these factors relate to depressive symptom burden among adolescent mothers in Juja Sub-County, Kiambu County. We surveyed 227 girls who had been pregnant or given birth at 10-19 years, drawn by stratified random sampling from a line list of 466 mapped across five wards. Trained assistants administered a structured questionnaire covering background characteristics, pregnancy and disclosure, stigma, and a seven-item depressive symptom checklist. Elevated symptom burden was set in advance at four or more endorsed items. Two logistic regression models examined factors linked to stigma (n = 199) and to elevated symptom burden (n = 184). Of those with parity data, 194 of 197 had already given birth. Most respondents were 17-19 years old (86.8%) and single (69.2%), 92.5% had no income of their own, and 47.1% had left school early. Nine in ten pregnancies (91.2%) were unplanned, and 41.4% of girls met anger, rejection or indifference when they first disclosed. Stigma was reported by 43.2%, elevated symptom burden by 27.1% and thoughts of self-harm by 16.4%. Only 27.3% had attended any support programme. Being single was the one factor associated with stigma (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] 3.50; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.48-8.31). Elevated symptom burden was associated with stigma (AOR 3.21; 1.54-6.69) and with an unsupportive disclosure reaction (AOR 2.54; 1.19-5.41), and was less likely with each additional year of age (AOR 0.69; 0.49-0.96). Programme attendance showed no association (AOR 0.89; 0.41-1.94). In this peri-urban community, depressive symptoms clustered among adolescent mothers who had been stigmatised or poorly received when they disclosed their pregnancy, and stigma tracked marital status more closely than poverty. Screening with validated tools at postnatal, child-health and antenatal visits, guidance for families and partners on responding to disclosure, and community work on attitudes to unmarried motherhood deserve testing in this setting.

after.authors: Li, S.; Ganss, E.; Gomez, C.; Lazarchak, A.; Moriarty, C.; McIntire, R.
after.abstract: Purpose - This study examines whether six health behaviors remain stable among high school students across the school year and whether associations between these behaviors recur across assessments. Design/methodology/approach - As part of a school health program evaluation, a pre-post longitudinal health survey was conducted among two samples of high school students in a U.S. vocational-technical high school. Study 1 surveyed 114 students from late winter to late spring in 2024. Study 2 surveyed 177 students from autumn 2024 to late spring 2025. Wilcoxon signed-rank tests examined group-level behavioral change, and Pearson correlation networks described associations among six health behaviors: sleep, breakfast consumption, physical activity, nature exposure, social media use, and mindfulness practices. Findings - The primary analyses detected no significant group-level changes in any of the six behaviors across either study interval, suggesting relative stability within these samples. A one-time survey may provide useful information for broad school health planning, whereas repeated assessment remains necessary for evaluating longer-term patterns or program effects. Sleep and breakfast showed the most consistent positive association. Physical activity and nature exposure were positively associated at three of the four assessments. Social media was isolated from the other behaviors at the first three assessments but was negatively associated with sleep and physical activity at the final assessment. Originality - The study distinguishes stability in group-level behavior from changes in the relationships among behaviors. The findings support efficient assessment for broad educational planning. They also identify behavior pairs that can be addressed together in school health education, including sleep and breakfast, physical activity and nature exposure, and social media, sleep, and physical activity.

after.authors: Zeng, H.; Athreya, S.; Dai, D.; Pleasure, M.; Ivezic, V.; Raman, S.; Marks, L.; Speier, W.; Arnold, C.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Department of Radiological Sciences, University of California, Los Angeles
after.abstract: Background: Repeated biopsies burden patients during prostate cancer active surveillance (AS). Existing MRI risk stratification tools avoiding biopsy remain limited by the difficulty of automated lesion segmentation. Purpose: To develop a model integrating gland MRI radiomics and clinicopathologic variables for predicting time to pathologic progression during prostate cancer AS. Materials and Methods: This retrospective single-institution study included men with grade group 1 or favorable grade group 2 prostate cancer undergoing AS with fusion-targeted and systematic biopsy (2010-2025). Gland segmentation used nnU-Net; gland radiomic features were selected by LASSO-penalized survival regression to train an XGBoost accelerated failure time model. Comparator models were assessed by C-index, time-dependent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), Kaplan-Meier, and decision curve analysis. Results: Of 522 men (median age, 64 years [IQR, 59-68]), 410 were assigned by site to development and 112 to internal testing. Gland segmentation Dice was 0.89 +/- 0.04. The C-index was higher for the gland radiomics model (0.77) than for clinicopathologic (0.68) and lesion radiomics (0.68) models (adjusted P [≤] .017), with the highest time-dependent AUC at 36 months (0.87 [95% CI: 0.78, 0.94]). Progression-free survival was lower in high-risk than low-risk groups (36 months, 63.9% vs 100%; 48 months, 55.4% vs 93.8%; log-rank P < .001). At a 0.25 risk threshold, 49.1% and 31.3% were low risk at 36 and 48 months (negative predictive value, 1.00; positive predictive value, 0.36). Conclusion: An automated gland radiomics model predicted time to pathologic progression during AS better than clinicopathologic and lesion-based models.

after.author_corresponding_institution: Department of Radiology, Shiga University of Medical Science Hospital
after.abstract: Purpose: To compare fine-tuned encoders, generative large language models (LLMs) and typed decisions (per-finding yes/no questions answered with a probability) for classifying 18 findings in chest CT reports, and to identify when typed decisions help. Methods: This retrospective study used public data. The internal test set comprised 150 CT-RATE reports with paired Japanese translations at three quality levels; the external test set, 243 naturally written Japanese reports with human annotations (RR-Findings). We compared ModernBERT encoders fine-tuned on 20,444 reports, generative LLMs (gpt-6-luna, Qwen3.8-27B, MedGemma), and typed decisions with Jev, the Decisions API and Qwen. Thresholds fixed on 450 development reports were applied unchanged externally. The primary metric was micro-F1; case-level paired bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated for 11 internal comparisons. Results: Encoders were best internally (English 0.9853; radiologist-checked Japanese 0.9576) and exceeded Jev (differences 0.0367, 95% CI 0.0258-0.0484; 0.0336, 0.0215-0.0464). Externally, Jev (0.8844) lay within the encoder seed range (0.8656-0.9144), exceeded the three generative conditions tested externally (best 0.8564) and the Decisions API (0.8177), and had the smallest internal-to-external decrease (-0.0396). An encoder trained on 2,044 reports reached 0.8226 externally. Typed-versus-generated differences changed direction across models and test sets. At a fixed threshold of 0.5, Jev fell to 0.7753 externally. Conclusion: Fine-tuned encoders performed best with ample in-distribution labels. Although threshold-dependent, Jev, with thresholds fitted on only 450 labeled reports, fell within the encoder seed range externally and exceeded the generative LLMs and an encoder trained on 2,044 reports, making it an option when labels are scarce.

after.author_corresponding_institution: Adigrat University College of Medicine and Health Sciences
after.abstract: Background: Poor adherence to Iron and folic acid (IFA) remains major public health challenge in Ethiopia. While national protocols advise IFA supplementation during pregnancy, adherence is low in the nation particularly in rural areas. In the study setting, there is lack of updated data regarding adherence to IFA and its determinant factors among pregnant women. Objective: To assess adherence to IFA supplements and associated factors among pregnant women in rural setting of Eastern Tigray, Ethiopia, 2025. Methods: A community-based cross-sectional study was carried out from March 2025 to April 2025 among 614 pregnant women in Eastern Tigray, Ethiopia. Simple random and systematic random sampling techniques were utilized to select districts and study participants respectively.  Data analysis was performed using SPSS 25, employing both binary and multivariable logistic regression. Multi-collinearity and goodness of fit tests were ensured using the variance inflation factor and Hosmer-Lemeshow test respectively. Statistical significance was declared at a p-value less than 0.05. Results:  A total of 599 participants were included and the prevalence of adherence to IFA Supplementation (IFAS) was 56% (95% CI: 52%, 60%). Having [≥] 4 ANC visits (AOR= 37.7 95% CI: 14.08 - 101.03), mothers with previous history of anemia (AOR=2.2 CI: 1.07 - 4.69), age of mothers [≥] 40 years (AOR= 11.5 CI: 1.06 - 124.05), mothers who received counseling about IFAS (AOR, 7.1; CI 3.24 - 15.37), and mothers travelled to the health facility 30 to 60 minutes and more than 60 minutes (AOR, 0.02; CI 0.01 - 0.04), and (AOR, 0.01(0 - 0.004), respectively had statistically significant association with adherence to IFAS. Conclusion: Women having four or more ANC visits, a previous history of anaemia, receiving counselling about IFAS, older age, and travelling less than 60 minutes to seek healthcare were associated with increased odds of adherence to IFAS.
